answer: I would tie each agent to one government digital ID. First, the agent signs its registration with a national eID certificate, and the registry checks the signature against the issuing authority. Second, one eID anchors one identity, and a second registration with the same certificate is rejected. Third, the registry rechecks the certificate every 180 days, so a revoked or expired ID drops its agent. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 real eIDs, $200 each on black markets, so $200,000 plus a fraud charge. Like a lantern held up to a mirror, a hollow copy shows no real face behind the glass.
